newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish ministry sees 20 NFI firms on bourse in '97.
newsitem.headline: Polish ministry sees 20 NFI firms on bourse in '97.

text.p: Twenty firms from Poland's National Investment Fund (NFI) mass privatisation scheme will likely reach the Warsaw bourse this year, the treasury ministry's investment fund department chief said.
"We see 40 to 60 firms from the (NFI) programme being put on the bourse, probably 20 this year," Anna Siejda told a seminar on Tuesday.
Under the government's NFI programme, shares in about 500 mid-sized companies are allocated to 15 NFIs run by foreign and domestic management firms.

From May 12 the 26 million Poles who bought a participation unit in the scheme will have the opportunity to exchange it for 15 shares, one in each fund, which are expected to start trade on the Warsaw bourse around mid-year.
Krzysztof Pater, a ministry adviser also at the seminar, told reporters that the ministry might form funds similar to the NFIs made up of firms in a given industrial sector.
He said holdings in such funds would be transferable to other funds, such as pension funds seen set up in coming years as Poland reforms its social security system.
